title: fix(app-shell): Studio resolves an app's own locale-map label in the designer locale instead of printing [object Object] (objectui#11181)
body:
Fixes #11181

Clause-②: no

## What

Studio's Interfaces pillar now prints an app's own `label` in the designer locale when that label is an inline locale map. Before, it printed `[object Object] · Navigation` as the navigation rail's heading. The Data pillar's Actions view reads an action's locale-map `label` the same way.

The spec types `AppSchema.label` and `ActionSchema.label` as `I18nLabel`: a plain string or an inline locale map. A plain-string label shows as authored, as before.

## Premise, verified on `origin/main` `37d166280` (after PR objectui#11187 merged)

- All four `String(` reads of the app's own label named on the card were present in `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`: two in the `resolvePackageApp` callback, two in `InterfacesPillar`'s app-load effect.
- `packageApp` (sites 1 and 2) is read in one place only, the topbar's `packageApp ? null : appDraftPending ? …` gate, so only its presence is read. A repo-wide `git grep -n packageApp` over non-test sources finds the declaration and that gate, nothing else.
- `appLabel` (sites 3 and 4) is read in one place, the rail heading's `tFormat('engine.studio.if.navHeading', …)`.
- `ObjectActionsPanel.labelText` resolved a map with a fixed key order of its own (`default`, `en-US`, `en`, `zh-CN`, then the first entry), without the locale. So under zh, a map carrying both languages showed its English text.

## How

- **Sites 3 and 4 (the rail heading).** `appLabel` now holds the label as the spec types it (`I18nLabel`). The heading resolves it at render: `navItemLabelText(appLabel, locale)`. The list-row read keeps its `label ?? name ?? packageId` order without `String()`. The body read takes `body.label ?? body.name` when either is present, and a body with neither keeps the list row's value. The old guard, `typeof body.label === 'string' || typeof body.name === 'string'`, let a map label beside a string name through into `String()`; it is gone.
- **Sites 1 and 2 (`packageApp`).** `packageApp.label` holds the raw `I18nLabel` the same way, with no `String()`.
- **`ObjectActionsPanel.labelText`** is now `label == null ? fallback : navItemLabelText(label, locale)`. The local key order is deleted. A plain string, the empty string included, is returned as authored, and an absent label still falls back to the action's name, as before. Only a map's entry choice changes: it is now the spec's `resolveI18nLabel` choice for the designer locale.

### The choice: hold the `I18nLabel`, resolve at render

I chose to resolve at render, as the dispatch preferred. The heading then follows a designer-language switch the way the nav rows beside it do, with no reload of the app. A pin measures this: the app's `layered` read count is unchanged across the switch.

For sites 1 and 2 there is no reader to resolve at, so I held the raw value there too. This is a deviation from the dispatch's suggested "resolve anyway", and here is why. Resolving inside `resolvePackageApp` would either freeze the text in the locale of the load, which is the stale-caption shape the card lists as out of scope, or add `locale` to the callback's dependencies, which would re-list the package's apps on every language switch. The `I18nLabel` type gives a future reader a compile error in the two sinks it would reach for: a JSX child, and a `tFormat` variable, whose type is string or number. That points the reader at the resolver. No `String()` of the label remains at either site.

### The helper's name

`navItemLabelText` (`metadata-admin/previews/navItemLabel.ts`) is reused, not forked. Its name misleads here: it is now the Studio's one `I18nLabel` reader for app and action labels too, not only nav items. I did not rename it, because the claim's file surface does not include that module or its other importers. It is recorded below as a naming note.

## Sweep of `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/` (every `String(` over a label)

Enumerated with `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD` on the directory, minus `*.test.*`, then `grep -n 'String('` in each file, with every hit read. The spec types are from a zod probe on the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0: `schema.shape.label.safeParse` of a two-language map. That map is accepted by `AppSchema` and `ActionSchema`, and refused by `ObjectSchema`, `FieldSchema`, `HookSchema`, `PermissionSetSchema` and `FlowSchema`.

| Site (by content) | Label of | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `resolvePackageApp`, the `list('app')` row | app | **fixed** (site 1) |
| `resolvePackageApp`, the first `listDrafts({ type: 'app' })` header | app | **fixed** (site 2) |
| `InterfacesPillar` app-load, the published list row | app | **fixed** (site 3) |
| `InterfacesPillar` app-load, the loaded body | app | **fixed** (site 4) |
| `ObjectActionsPanel.labelText` (a local key-order resolver, not a `String(` read) | action | **folded** onto `navItemLabelText` |
| `loadPackageObjects` | object | excluded: `ObjectSchema.label` is a string |
| `InterfacesPillar` package-objects effect | object | excluded: `ObjectSchema.label` is a string |
| `DataPillar` rail load | object | excluded: `ObjectSchema.label` is a string |
| `PackageOwdOverviewPanel`, the published-label map and the row label | object | excluded: `ObjectSchema.label` is a string |
| `ObjectFormDesigner.fieldLabelOf` | field | excluded: `FieldSchema.label` is a string |
| `ObjectHooksPanel`, the saved toast and the pane title (`String(draft.label \|\| draft.name)`) | hook | excluded: `HookSchema.label` is a string |
| `AccessPillar` rail load | permission set | excluded: `PermissionSetSchema.label` is a string |
| `packageSurfaces.loadPackageSurfaces` (its only caller passes `'flow'`) | flow | excluded: `FlowSchema.label` is a string |
| `InterfacesPillar` app-load, `label = String(d.name)` on a draft header | — | not a label read: it is the draft's `name` |
| the `StudioDesignSurface` comment quoting the retired `String(label ?? title ?? name)` | — | prose, not a read |

## Tests

New pins:

- `StudioDesignSurface.interfacesAppLabelMap-11181.test.tsx` has 8 tests. It renders the real `InterfacesPillar` over a mocked metadata client, the harness of the objectui#11158 rail test. The app fixtures parse against `AppSchema`. Under en and under zh it checks three things. After the body loads, a map-labelled app's heading reads `Acme · Navigation` or `顶点 · 导航` (site 4). While the body read is held open, the list row alone gives the same heading (site 3). The plain-string control prints as authored. One more test switches the designer language from en to zh and checks that the heading changes without re-reading the app.
- `ObjectActionsPanel.labelMap-11181.test.tsx` has 3 tests. The action fixtures parse against `ActionSchema`. Under en and zh, the map-labelled action's list row and its detail pane show the designer-locale entry and not the other language's, and the plain-string action is shown as authored.

Ablation: one leg per site family, run after the fix was committed. Each leg went through `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, and a script trap restored both files as well. Each mutation was confirmed on disk (anchor count 1 to 0, blob changed). After each leg the restore was proven with blob equal to `HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

| Leg | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | site 4 back to the old `typeof` guard and `String(body.label ?? body.name ?? label)` | 3 failed, 5 passed: the body-loaded en and zh tests (heading read `[object Object] · Navigation` / `[object Object] · 导航`) and the language-switch test |
| A2 | site 3 back to `String(published[0].label ?? …)` | 2 failed, 6 passed: the list-row en and zh tests |
| A3 | site 4 resolves once at load, `setAppLabel(navItemLabelText(bodyLabel, locale))` | 1 failed, 7 passed: only the language-switch test |
| C1 | `labelText` back to its local key order | 1 failed, 2 passed: only the zh test (it shows `Send Email`) |
| sites 1–2 | — | **NOT MEASURED**: nothing reads `packageApp.label`, so neither a test nor the type-checker can observe the site |

Local gates, run at `d26b5a97b` (the head this PR opens with):

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/`: 75 files and 425 tests passed. That is the whole directory, including both `ObjectActionsPanel` suites.
- `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: 28 of 28 tasks succeeded. Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exited 0. The script name `type-check` is echoed in the output. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists both new test files.
- `eslint` on the 4 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files, run as the package's `lint` script runs it (`eslint .`, inline config honoured): 0 errors. The 18 warnings on `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` are also 18 on the base file.
  - This is a declared narrowing from the package's `eslint .`. The file count comes from `--format json`. `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, and no rule in `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem. So the diff cannot move a verdict on any untouched file.
- `check-changeset-presence`, `-no-major`, `-fixed`, `-overwrite`, `-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:vi-mock-specifiers` / `-inherit` / `-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check-type-check-coverage` and `markdown-test-inputs --audit`: all exit 0.
- The root `scripts/__tests__/` suite was run once because the diff adds a changeset (markdown): `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 scripts/__tests__/` passed 177 files (2 skipped) and 5371 tests (2 skipped).

## Acceptance notes

- **Naming.** `navItemLabelText` now serves app and action labels as well. A rename such as `i18nLabelText` would touch `navItemLabel.ts` and its importers `AppNavCanvas`, `navSurface` and `StudioDesignSurface`. Carrier: none (no PR or person is set to touch that file).
- `check-changeset-claims` flagged the pending `.changeset/6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`, because its paragraph names `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`. I read that paragraph. It describes chunk co-tenancy of the marketplace imports, and this diff adds no import, so it is still true.
- Not measured, per the triage: the canvas caption after a designer-language switch or a nav rename (read in source only on the card). That stays out of scope here.
